rejected.title: Lower costs
card: A business has a cost advantage when it can make its goods or services for less than its rivals. It can then charge lower prices, or keep more profit from each sale.
Research can find cheaper materials or better ways to make a product. Efficient methods, such as cutting waste or using machines well, lower the cost of each item.
Local resources, such as nearby raw materials or workers, can cut the cost of transport and supply.
Outsourcing means paying another business to do a task, such as making parts or answering calls. It can be cheaper when that business can do the task for less.
rejected.remember: A business with lower costs can cut prices or earn more profit on each sale.

a.q: Why does a lower cost of production help a business compete?
opts: It can charge less or keep more profit per sale
It makes its product different from every rival
It guarantees that customers will be loyal to it
It means the business no longer needs to advertise
a.why: Lower costs let a business set a lower price than rivals or earn more on each sale. Making a product different is a separate way to compete, and cheaper production does not do that by itself.
a.clue: Think about what a business can do with money saved on each item.

b.q: Tom runs a furniture workshop in Tasmania. He buys timber from a mill nearby, which saves him freight costs. Which way of lowering costs is this?
opts: Using local resources
Outsourcing a task
Doing research
Using efficient methods
b.why: Tom is saving money because the timber is close by, so this is the use of local resources. It is not outsourcing, because he is buying a material and not paying another business to do a task for him.
b.clue: Where does the saving come from: the timber's location or a new task done by someone else?

version.title: Lower costs
card: A business can compete by producing more cheaply than its rivals. It can then charge a lower price, or keep its price and earn more profit on each sale.
Research can find cheaper materials or a better way to make a product. Efficient methods make more with the same inputs, such as by wasting fewer materials.
Using local resources, such as materials found nearby, can cut the cost of transport.
Outsourcing means paying another business to do a task, such as delivery or cleaning. It saves money when that business can do the task for less.
version.remember: Find a cheaper way to produce, and you can beat rivals on price or on profit.

a.q: A business finds a way to make each item for less than its rivals do. How can this help it compete?
opts: It can sell for less than rivals and still profit
It can stop rivals from selling the same item
It can charge more because its items cost less
It can skip advertising as costs are now lower
a.why: With a lower cost for each item, a business can set a lower price than its rivals and still make a profit, which draws customers. Charging more is the reverse: lower costs make lower prices possible, not higher ones.
a.clue: What can a business do with the money it saves on each item?

b.q: Kai makes surfboards in Margaret River. He now pays a courier company to deliver his boards, because it costs less than running his own van. Which way of lowering costs is this?
opts: Outsourcing a task
Using local resources
Doing research
Using efficient methods
b.why: Kai pays another business to do a task, delivery, because it costs less than doing it himself. That is outsourcing. It is not using local resources, because the saving comes from someone else doing the work, not from nearby materials.

a.best: It can sell for less than rivals and still profit
